# synology_snmp (Resource)

SNMP service configuration. Import adopts current settings without writing. Secrets are write-only, require import and change only through Update when their version increases; external secret changes cannot be drift-detected. Destroy never changes DSM. Applied secret-generation baselines are protected; release them explicitly with a removed block using destroy = false. Protocol settings are available only while the corresponding service is active.

## Adopt existing settings

Use an initialized project from [Check the NAS connection](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/elephant-evergreen/synology/latest/docs#check-the-nas-connection). Add this import block with your resource address and the ID of the existing DSM object.

```terraform
import {
  to = synology_snmp.main
  id = "snmp"
}
```

1. Add the resource block with the values DSM currently reports. Use the sample configuration as a starting point.
2. Run `terraform plan -out=adopt.tfplan`. For one import, expect `1 to import, 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy`. If the plan proposes changes, match the differing arguments to DSM and save a new plan.
3. Run `terraform apply adopt.tfplan` once the saved plan contains only the import. The next `terraform plan` should report `No changes`.

## Example configuration

```terraform
resource "synology_snmp" "main" {
  enabled         = false
  v1_v2_enabled   = false
  v3_enabled      = false
  privacy_enabled = false
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `auth_protocol` (String) SNMP v3 authentication: MD5 or SHA. Configure only with enabled v3; omission preserves the observed value.
- `authentication_password_version` (Number) Increase to apply authentication_password_wo. Zero preserves the imported secret. An acknowledged write checkpoints this counter before readback. This does not detect external secret changes.
- `authentication_password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Write-only SNMP secret. Supply it with an increased authentication_password_version. Omit during import. Never persisted in plan or state.
- `community_version` (Number) Increase to apply community_wo. Zero preserves the imported secret. An acknowledged write checkpoints this counter before readback. This does not detect external secret changes.
- `community_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Write-only SNMP secret. Supply it with an increased community_version. Omit during import. Never persisted in plan or state.
- `contact` (String) SNMP system contact.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable the SNMP service.
- `location` (String) SNMP system location.
- `name` (String) SNMP system name.
- `privacy_enabled` (Boolean) Enable SNMP v3 privacy. An inactive service with no returned privacy flag is represented as false.
- `privacy_password_version` (Number) Increase to apply privacy_password_wo. Zero preserves the imported secret. An acknowledged write checkpoints this counter before readback. This does not detect external secret changes.
- `privacy_password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Write-only SNMP secret. Supply it with an increased privacy_password_version. Omit during import. Never persisted in plan or state.
- `privacy_protocol` (String) SNMP v3 privacy: DES or AES. Configure only with enabled privacy; omission preserves the observed value.
- `username` (String) Read-only SNMP v3 user name.
- `v1_v2_enabled` (Boolean) Enable SNMP v1/v2c.
- `v3_enabled` (Boolean) Enable SNMP v3.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Singleton identity and import identifier: snmp. Destroy only releases Terraform management; it never resets DSM settings.
- `reconciliation_required` (Boolean) Terraform lifecycle guard for a secret write whose acknowledgement is uncertain. Inspect DSM and explicitly reconcile before retry or replacement; this is local lifecycle metadata, not a DSM setting.
